messages:
customer_acme: Hey team — we started seeing streaming responses get cut off about ~10% of the time. Node client (fetch) gets a final short chunk, then connection closes; server logs show 499. Payload is valid JSON but truncated in the last object. Happening behind our nginx proxy (aws alb -> nginx -> app). Repro steps below.

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro and the SDK + server version? Also whether you're using the JS SDK or raw EventSource/fetch SSE.

customer_acme: Using our in-house wrapper around fetch with keepalive:true. Not using Redwood JS SDK directly. Node 18.16, Ubuntu 22.04, nginx 1.22.1. App runs an express route that proxies to Redwood streaming endpoint `/v1/stream`. Repro gist: 

```js
// repro-client.js (Node)
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const controller = new AbortController();
fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-open-2', prompt: 'lots of tokens' }),
  signal: controller.signal,
  keepalive: true
}).then(res => {
  res.body.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk));
  res.body.on('end', () => console.log('end'));
});
```

nginx proxy conf (snip): `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection '';`

maria_support: Thanks — can you also grab a raw tcp capture of one truncated stream (first ~2s) and the app/nginx logs? Also which Redwood API URL are you hitting (hosted vs private)?

customer_acme: It's our Private deployment (VPC) in eu-west-1. Attached snippets in the ticket but here are the app logs around the time: 

```
[2026-02-15T14:02:11Z] upstream response started id=abc123
[2026-02-15T14:02:12Z] chunk sent size=1024
[2026-02-15T14:02:12Z] chunk sent size=512
[2026-02-15T14:02:12Z] upstream closed: code=499
[2026-02-15T14:02:12Z] client aborted, conn=4321
```

customer_acme: The client reported `end` but last log line from the stream indicates we probably didn't flush final buffer from Redwood.

jonathan_eng: I can take a look. 499 from nginx likely means the client closed before the upstream finished; could be because node's keepalive + proxy connection re-use triggers an early socket close when stream finishes and client uses `res.destroy()` implicitly. Any pattern about larger prompts vs smaller?

customer_acme: Larger prompts more likely, and it seems correlated with bursts (when we have concurrent streams ~>10). Single stream is usually fine.

akash_dev: Two quick checks: 1) Are you using `res.body.on('close')` anywhere to abort? 2) Can you try setting `agent: false` or using a new agent per request to rule out socket re-use? Also which Node fetch impl — undici or node-fetch? That can matter for keepalive.

customer_acme: We're on `undici` 5.14.0 via node 18 builtin. We do not explicitly `destroy()` the stream. Using a shared Agent.

olivia_sre: Pinging deploy-bot to check if any edge LB connection churn aligned with those timestamps.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] No deployments around 2026-02-15T14:00-14:10. No LB restart events.

jonathan_eng: Ok here's something I repro'd locally with an nginx reverse-proxy and undici agent. When the client (Node undici) finishes reading and the proxy unbuffers, there's a timing window where the connection can be half-closed: server thinks it sent final chunk, proxy reuses the socket while client's TLS session still in teardown -> upstream sees ECONNRESET and logs client aborted. On our side (Redwood runtime) we log stream complete but kernel-level write returns EPIPE before the last flush. That can cause the client's Received bytes to miss final flush.

akash_dev: There's also a known bug in undici where `keepalive` + stream + concurrent sockets can trigger early FIN when socket pool is saturated (we saw it in a past internal ticket). Workaround: disable connection pool reuse per request (new Agent) or switch to a streaming-capable SDK wrapper that drains the socket fully before returning.

maria_support: For customers using the JS stack behind nginx, our temporary recommended mitigations are: 
- set `agent: new Agent({ connections: 0 })` / disable keepalive re-use per request
- set `proxy_buffering on` to avoid nginx freeing too early (if acceptable)
- upgrade undici to latest patch that addresses socket shutdown (if available)

customer_acme: Can you provide a small code snippet for the Agent workaround?

jonathan_eng: Sure: 
```js
const { Agent } = require('undici');
const agent = new Agent({ connections: 1 }); // new pool per client instance
fetch(url, { agent })
```

akash_dev: Also try toggling `Connection: close` on nginx -> sets no reuse. Not ideal for perf but useful to validate.

customer_acme: I tried `agent: new Agent({ connections: 1 })` and increased client concurrency. Reproductions dropped from ~12% to ~0.5% over 1k runs. That's a huge improvement.

maria_support: Great — we'll ship a KB article with repro and mitigations. We'll also escalate to runtime team to see if we can make the server flush/ack behavior more resilient to mid-TCP shutdowns. Tagging @jonathan_eng to follow up.

jonathan_eng: Filed internal ticket RUNTIME-STREAM-4723. Plan: add extra socket drain/confirmation on final chunk write and a short retry for transient EPIPE during final flush (non-duplicative). Risk low, but need to validate with our congestion tests.

akash_dev: Also adding note to JS SDK docs: avoid global keepalive agent for heavy concurrent streaming behind proxies, or provide a streaming-safe Agent wrapper.

customer_acme: Thanks all — we'll keep the agent workaround in place. Can you add me to the internal ticket for updates? (customer email threaded in the support ticket).

maria_support: Yep — added contact. Closing here with mitigation in place. Will follow up once runtime change lands. :thumbsup:
